summary: Pair 4 clears the strict bar across all six scored categories. E1.4 is faithfully addressed and the lesson explicitly bridges to Lesson 3 (congruence yesterday) and Lesson 5 (capstone mirror-maze), with curriculum text byte-identical to input_row.json. The expanded_walkthrough names the side-view-vs-top-down perspective trap, cites Liben & Downs (1989) and Battista on spatial perspective-taking, and supplies three diagnostic-branched recovery_moves (A side-view repair via phone-camera demo, B scale drill, C symbol-key drill). Materials are everyday (anchor chart, paper map template, symbol cards); Symmy and Flippy puppets are explicitly OPTIONAL with voice/stuffed-animal/paper-bag fallbacks, and a NO-PAPER walk-and-say path is named in differentiation_for_movement_learners. Time 12/25/13 = 50 min sits in the G2 band. The Symmy + Flippy refrain 'Top-down, top-down, that's how MAPS look!' opens the hook and closes the exit_routine as a chant. Mathematical authenticity is anchored by a STRATEGY COMPARE step where two pairs compare bedroom-map symbol choices and Symmy names the math principle ('Different symbols, same TOP-DOWN view. The MATH cares about the perspective'), with Liben & Downs (1989) cited by name. Worksheet Part 1 deliberately varies the practice context (kitchen or library top-down map) rather than the bedroom rehearsed in the lesson, and teacher_notes justifies this as a transfer check for map-reading generalization.
